name: The Explosion
label: Revelation
lede: A Boston punk band sold 250 demo tapes on a Kid Dynamite tour, made one of Spin's favorite records of 2000, paid off a label's legal threat with an EP, and then watched Virgin shelve the album that was supposed to finish the job.

eras.title: Two hundred and fifty tapes
eras.text: The Explosion came together in Boston in fall 1998 through the Big Wheel Recreation crowd, with a bassist fresh from the straight edge band In My Eyes. A homemade demo and a tour with Kid Dynamite were enough to get them a record deal.

years.p: Matt Hock and ex-In My Eyes bassist Damian Genuardi meet guitarist David Walsh through Rama Mayo of Big Wheel Recreation. Drummer Dan Colby and guitarist Sam Cave, from the band Trouble, join soon after.

years.h: 250 demo tapes on the road with Kid Dynamite
years.p: The Explosion press 250 copies of their demo and sell them on tour with [[Kid Dynamite|c5300096-cfb0-4801-b146-166e2d02f08a]]. The tour leads straight to a deal with Jade Tree.

eras.title: Jade Tree, Spin, and a lawsuit threat
eras.text: The Explosion's debut album landed on Spin's list of the top 20 albums of 2000. That success brought an unexpected claim from Revelation Records, the label that still had Damian Genuardi's old band.

years.p: The Explosion's first release collects six songs from the demo they sold on the Kid Dynamite tour.

years.h: Flash Flash Flash, one of Spin's top 20 of 2000
years.p: Fourteen songs in about 27 minutes, recorded in February 2000 and opening with No Revolution. Spin names it one of the top 20 albums of the year.
years.xp: The Washington Post heard it as a record from the open-nerve stage of adolescence. Robert Christgau gave it a choice-cut mention. The track list includes Reactor, Terrorist and Tarantulas Attack.

years.big: One EP to keep the bassist's name on the records
years.src: Wikipedia: Steal This · Wikipedia: The Explosion · Revelation Records pressing history
years.h: Steal This: the EP that settled Revelation's claim
years.p: Revelation, which had Damian Genuardi's old band In My Eyes, threatened to sue him if he was credited on Explosion records. The band settled by giving Revelation an EP, Steal This (REV 98).
years.xp:
According to Wikipedia, Revelation believed The Explosion's success on Jade Tree should belong to it. The band wrote the EP on tour, and it isn't counted among their best work.

Revelation's first pressing: 300 red and 1,975 black copies. In My Eyes' own albums on Revelation were REV 67 (1998) and REV 80 (1999).

years.h: The Explosion on the Warped Tour
years.p: The Explosion play the 2001 Warped Tour, part of years of touring the US and Europe with [[AFI|1c3919b2-43ca-4a4a-935d-9d50135ec0ef]], [[Alkaline Trio|69421e11-e4c3-4854-951b-ceab4972e38e]], [[Social Distortion|e1e05cce-3922-44e1-8f20-015abe5e309d]], [[The (International) Noise Conspiracy|97da5eb3-79a5-4195-b98e-3d10ef946b08]] and [[Rocket from the Crypt|e297ecdf-64ec-4e34-899d-80380f5b0c2a]].

years.h: Location Is Everything, Vol. 1 on Jade Tree
years.p: Jade Tree's Location Is Everything, Vol. 1 compilation includes The Explosion alongside the label's roster.

eras.title: Virgin, and the album nobody heard
eras.text: The Explosion went from self-releasing to a major label in a year. Then Virgin let them finish a second album for the company, dropped them, and the band called it quits.

years.h: Sick of Modern Art EP on Tarantulas Records
years.p: Between labels, The Explosion put out the Sick of Modern Art EP on Tarantulas Records.

years.h: Black Tape, The Explosion's Virgin Records debut
years.p: The Explosion's major-label debut comes out on Virgin, with the Red Tape EP on Tarantulas alongside it.

years.h: Live in Boston and a second Warped Tour
years.p: Instant Live releases The Explosion's Live in Boston, and the band returns to the Warped Tour. Virgin issues Here I Am and No Revolution as singles.

years.h: New drummer and guitarist for The Explosion
years.p: Andrew Black replaces drummer Dan Colby, and Chris Gonzalez, formerly of [[Let It Burn|71a59653-b14e-4e6f-9ac5-28472638fd31]], replaces guitarist Sam Cave.

years.h: Virgin drops The Explosion after Bury Me Standing
years.p: The Explosion finish a second Virgin album, Bury Me Standing, and Virgin drops them from the roster. The record goes unreleased.
The Explosion post the news on their website and book a last run of shows.

years.h: The Explosion's last show, in New York
years.p: The Explosion play their final show in New York, nine years after forming in Boston.

eras.title: Bury Me Standing, finally
eras.text: The Explosion kept coming back for short runs, and the album Virgin had buried came out five years late. From 2019 they were a working band again, opening for Bad Religion.

years.p: The Explosion play their first shows since the 2007 split.

years.h: Bury Me Standing released, five years after Virgin shelved it
years.p: The album The Explosion finished for Virgin in early 2007 comes out at last on Valentine's Day 2012.

years.h: The Explosion back for good, touring with Bad Religion
years.p: After one-off reunions in 2014 and 2016, The Explosion return as an active band with Andrew Black and Chris Gonzalez, including tours supporting [[Bad Religion|149e6720-4e4a-41a4-afca-6d29083fc091]].
